llm.summary: This skill is mostly a disclosed router for AI KEY workflows, but it asks the agent to inventory local skills and reveal real filesystem paths, so it needs review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill looks in ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills, and repository locations, then prints installed aikey skill names, descriptions, and real source paths. It also relies on local vault/config/memory files for the broader workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package includes an executable read-only shell script, artifact/scripts/list-skills.sh, used for discovery. It does not install services, fetch remote payloads, or modify tools during installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Trigger phrases include broad everyday requests such as asking what to shoot or how to use the tool, which can activate routing and local discovery in conversations where the user may not have intended environment inspection.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No privilege escalation or system-level persistence was found. The referenced family rules do define local memory and output-file writes for the workflow, including automatic feedback records, which are disclosed but should be understood before use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose as a content/business skill router is coherent, but the capability extends into shell-based local skill discovery, reading other installed skill manifests, and surfacing true source paths, which is broader than minimal routing needs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill reading local AI KEY-related configuration, memory, and installed-skill metadata, and with it using a shell script to list installed aikey skills and their real paths. Prefer explicit /aikey commands over broad natural-language triggers, and review the local vault/memory behavior before using it with private business or content data.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Dynamic discovery of installed aikey skills supports the router purpose, but exposing real source paths is unnecessary for user-facing routing and creates a local environment disclosure concern.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad natural-language triggers are genuinely overbroad for a router that may run local discovery, increasing accidental activation risk.
[AE1] expected: The packaged references were available for inspection, but the runtime design intentionally reads selected downstream skills that may be installed separately; that limits what this package review can validate.
[SDI-1] expected: The onboarding mode performs a small demo-grade analysis despite the router boundary. This is disclosed as the exception for new users and is not independently malicious.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The onboarding free-form triggers are also broad and can enter guided mode without a namespaced command.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The shell script is read-only and purpose-related, but running it from a conversational router to enumerate installed skills and print paths is overbroad.
[SDI-4] expected: The apparent onboarding contradiction is mostly a handoff: option 1 exits the compressed demo and runs normal Mode A routing. It should be clearer, but the artifact does not show hidden execution beyond the selected workflow.
